İnsani Gelişme Endeksi: The composite statistic developed by the United Nations in 1990, measuring life expectancy, education and income levels together.
İpotek: A type of lien that can be accepted as collateral by banks particularly in return for commercial credits, placed on the real estate at an amount reaching 1.5 or 2 times the credit debt. Right of Easement: a legal person's obtaining the right of use over lands not belonging to itself.
İradi işsizlik ya da sürtünmesel işsizli: The type of unemployment stemming from individuals' entering and leaving the labor market and their temporary waits between jobs.
İskonto: Refers to a credit transaction enabling the purchase of commercial bills before their maturity and their conversion into cash with certain discounts.
İskonto oranı: The interest rate used in converting future cash flows into present value; it reflects the opportunity cost and the risk premium.
İslami Finansal Hizmetler Kurulu: An international organization that began its activities in 2003 with the aims of establishing international regulatory standards for Islamic financial institutions in the fields of banking, securities markets and insurance so as to encourage the development of the Islamic financial services sector, providing guidance on the effective supervision of institutions offering Islamic financial products, and developing criteria for the identification, measurement, management and disclosure of risks for the Islamic financial services sector.
İstatistiksel fark: The inconsistency formed among interrelated calculations owing to the components in macroeconomics that cannot be measured precisely and instantaneously.
İsteklerin karşılıklı örtüşmesi: The situation in which the objects one person wants to give and take are the same as the objects another person wants to take and give in return.
İsteğe bağlı maliye politikası: Fiscal policies decided upon by policymakers and put into implementation when necessary.
İstihdamda olan ya da çalışan: The persons engaged, in a given period, in any activity directed toward production or the provision of services with the aim of earning a wage or profit.
İstikrarlı Fonlama Oranı: The funding rate the CBRT makes with its one-week repo auctions is defined as 'Steady Funding Rate 1', and the interest on the borrowing facility granted to market-maker banks through repo operations within the framework of open market operations is defined as 'Steady Funding Rate 2'.
İtfa: The repayment of the accrued interest and the principal of debt securities at the maturity date determined at their issuance.
İthalat: The buying of goods from other countries by the persons and institutions resident in a country.
İthalat fonksiyonu: The mathematical relationship showing how the quantity of imports changes, depending on various variables, in an economy.
İtibari değer: The amount to be paid at maturity to the person holding the bond.
İyi mal: Products that provide benefit to economic units and whose price in the market is positive.
İç borç: The total amount of debt the state has received from households and firms resident domestically.
İç verim oranı: The discount rate that makes the NPV zero; it is expected to exceed the project's cost of capital. When the IRR and the NPV conflict, the NPV is taken as the basis.
İş bulma ümidi olmayan: Persons who previously searched for work and no longer search because they do not believe they can find a job suitable for themselves, but who are ready to start work.
İş Yapma Kolaylığı Endeksi: The Doing Business Index, prepared regularly every year since 2004 by the World Bank, analyzes the business regulations affecting the investment climate in member countries. İŞGEM: Business Development Centers whose establishment criteria and qualities are determined by KOSGEB. İŞKUR: the Turkish Employment Agency (İŞKUR), the relevant organization of the Ministry of Family, Labor and Social Services, whose activities are the preservation, development and spread of employment and the prevention of unemployment
İş çevrimi: Or economic fluctuation: the ups and downs seen in total production, income and expenditures within periods of a few years in market economies.
İşbirliği modeli: The oligopoly model in which different sellers come together and make their price-output choices in explicit or tacit cooperation.
İşgücü: Those among the population of working age who enter the labor force by showing a desire to work are accepted as being in the labor force. The total of those who are seeking work but have not yet found work — in other words, those in the unemployed position — and of those who are employed constitutes the labor force.
İşgücü piyasası ya da emek piyasası: The physical or virtual environment where those who supply labor and those who demand labor come together, and in this process the wage rate of labor is determined.
İşgücüne Katılma Oranı: The ratio of the labor force to the population of working age.
İşgücüne yapılan ödeme: The incomes such as salaries and wages that labor obtains in the production process.
İşlem güdüsü: The demand for money stemming from the need for cash for daily shopping.
İşletme artığı: The incomes such as profit, interest and rent that capital and land obtain in the production process.
İşsiz: Persons who have no job, who are seeking work, and who have made efforts in this direction are defined as unemployed.
İşsizlik: Or excess labor supply: the situation in which the quantity of labor supplied in the labor market exceeds the quantity demanded.
İşsizlik Oranı: Defined as the ratio of the unemployed to the labor force.
İşsizlik sigortası: The compulsory insurance that covers, for a certain period and to a certain extent, the income loss suffered by persons who lose their jobs without fault of their own.
J-eğrisi etkisi: The phenomenon of net exports first decreasing and then beginning to increase as the exchange rate rises.
Jensen alfası: The difference of the portfolio from the return predicted by the CAPM: α = Rp − [Rf + β(Rm − Rf)]; a positive alpha is counted as manager value added.
Joint Profit Maximization: The members in formations such as cartels, duopolies and oligopolies taking their price and production decisions in the way that will maximize the profit of the whole group.
Kadastro: The work of determining, by the state and tying to a plan, the locations, areas, boundaries, values and legal statuses of all the lands, plots and properties in a country, with the aim of establishing an orderly and sound land registry. Leverage Ratio: the ratio showing what part of an enterprise's assets are financed with foreign resources.
Kaldor-Hicks etkinliği: The allocation of resources in which, while improving the situation of some individuals, the harm of the individuals whose situation worsens is compensated as far as possible.
Kalkınma Planı: Long-term plans, the first of which entered into force in 1963, offering a road map in national development, mandatory for the public sector and directive for the private sector.
Kalkınma ve yatırım bankası: The public bank established to meet the financing needs of entrepreneurs in line with Türkiye's sustainable development priorities, to contribute to the broadening of capital across the base and to structural transformation, and to provide consultancy support.
Kamu Alım Garantisi: A business model in which the state gives a purchase commitment, with the aim of encouraging the private sector and enabling investments to be made with less financing need.
Kamu borcu: The total of the state's internal debts and external debts.
Kamu Kaynaklı Finansman: The covering, using public resources, of the losses arising during the resolution of a financial institution.
Kamu Kesimi Borçlanma Gereği: The general balance of the public sector covering the central government budget, local administrations, SOEs, extra-budgetary funds, social security institutions, the unemployment insurance fund, organizations with revolving funds and general health insurance.
Kamu malı: Goods that are non-excludable in consumption and create no rivalry.
Kamu Net Borç Stoku: Refers to the public sector net debt stock calculated by subtracting the financial assets held by the public sector from the total of the public sector's internal and external debt liabilities.
Kamu Yararı Kararı: The decision preceding the expropriation decision, initiating the expropriation transaction and approved by the competent authorities, required for the administration to be able to decide on expropriation.
Kamulaştırma: The transaction of the registration, in the name of the administration, of the entirety or a part of the real estates in the ownership of real and private-law legal persons, or of the easement right, by the state or public legal persons, in cases where the public benefit requires it, on the condition of paying its consideration in advance.
Kapalı ekonomi: A self-sufficient economy that does not trade with the outside world to a considerable degree.
Kapasite fazlası: The inability to produce in the way that makes average total cost minimal, owing to the production factors at hand not being fully used.
Kapasite Kullanım Oranı: An indicator relating the actual capacity utilizations of workplaces operating in the manufacturing industry to their existing physical capacities.
